subtitle: 偷人是门技术活
sentences: It was the first time I'd realized there were different ways to rescue someone.
For instance, I said, "We could hide them in the vegetable cart," and Wen Li said, "No."
I said, "Then we'll dress up as officers," and Uncle Qin said, "No."
I suggested bribing the gate guards, and Mother simply pushed her abacus across the table.
"First, work out how many shops Jiang Trading House would have left if the bribe came to light."
I quietly pushed the abacus back.
"Mother, we can't just stand by while they're left to starve in the marquis's residence, can we?"
"Aren't you supposed to be delivering medicine?" she said. "Then deliver medicine properly. Ask whether they'll accept it first. Stop seeing every doorway as something to sneak through."

Uncle Qin nodded beside her. "The Jiang family delivers vegetables to the rear kitchen every day. Those deliveries go on the supply books. They only count as delivered when the kitchen signs for them. The cart can reach the back lane; the driver can't wander into whichever courtyard he pleases."
Wen Li added, "And Nanny Zhou's husband is ill. Even if they do want to leave, a doctor needs to see whether he's fit to be moved."
I looked at the three people sitting around the table and had the distinct feeling I'd transmigrated into the wrong book.
In other stories, the villainess outsmarts her enemies one day and takes charge of the imperial harem the next.
In mine, I tried to save two people and ended up sitting through three rounds of risk assessment.
Still, there were preparations to make.

Uncle Qin found us Doctor Fang, who saw patients at a clinic in the western part of town. A-Qin sent word that Uncle Feng was feverish and barely aware of his surroundings, with a terrible cough. Nanny Zhou wanted a doctor to examine him inside the residence. She had no intention of abandoning her husband and escaping alone.
At least this time, I knew what she wanted for herself.
The next morning, the wind in the back lane was cold and damp.

I wore a coarse-cloth apron and sat beside Chuntao on the vegetable cart. Wen Li waited at the pharmacy next door for news, while Uncle Qin and Doctor Fang stayed at the mouth of the lane. All we meant to do was deliver the medicine and see whether there was a chance to speak to someone in the rear courtyard.
As usual, a guard stopped the cart at the gate.
"Leave today's vegetables outside. You're not taking them in."
The driver blinked. "We usually take them to the kitchen to be weighed. If we leave them here, who's going to sign for them?"
"Someone inside will come and collect them."
"And if two baskets of radishes go missing, whose account does that go on?" I lifted the cart curtain. "Yours?"
The guard looked me up and down. "And who might you be?"
"I keep the Jiang family's accounts."
One look at my apron told me he didn't believe a word of it.
"The bookkeeper delivers vegetables herself?"

"Our accounting office has been sealed, and we're short-handed. I'm not going to force my way in. But someone has to count the goods. If your kitchen later claims we're short on weight, how am I supposed to explain that to Mother?"
I'd barely finished when a round-faced steward emerged from the gate, his expression darker than the bottom of a cooking pot.
"We'll accept the Jiang family's goods as usual. Stop making a scene out here. When has the Xie household ever shortchanged you?"
"Of last month's thirteen cartloads of vegetables, two are still unpaid," I said at once, repeating what Uncle Qin had made me memorize. "Since you're here, could you settle those as well?"
The steward was lost for words.
Chuntao gave my arm a discreet pinch, warning me not to push my luck.
Just then, a fit of coughing came from inside the courtyard. Even through the wall, it sounded as though something was lodged deep in the sufferer's chest.

I saw a gray-haired woman pushing a little wooden barrow through the gateway, an old brown jacket draped over her shoulders. She didn't look our way. She merely stopped and bent to retrieve a packet of medicine from the ground.
"Nanny Zhou!" the guard barked. "Who gave you permission to come here?"
She slowly straightened up.
"The kitchen asked me to bring back the old baskets."
"We don't need you for that."
Nanny Zhou rested a hand on the barrow's handle, her knuckles standing out sharply. I suddenly remembered what Wen Li had said: she hadn't set out to be a hero. She just wanted her family to be safe.
Not one of the thirty argumentative lines I'd prepared would come out.

Chuntao took a small packet from beneath the vegetable baskets. Doctor Fang had prepared some ordinary fever-relieving herbs based on A-Qin's description of the symptoms; the outside carried a warning to seek an examination and not take them without medical advice.
"Nanny," she said softly, "someone asked us to bring this to you."
Nanny Zhou didn't reach for it. First she looked at the steward, then at us.
"The marquis's household isn't short of medicine," the steward said.

"All the better," I said. "The doctor we brought is waiting at the end of the lane. With someone coughing like that, surely you can let him take a look. If there's really no shortage of medicine, at least we'll have done what we were asked."
The steward's face changed. "Who told you to bring a doctor?"
"Nobody," I said. "Just a vegetable seller sticking her nose where it doesn't belong."
"This is the marquis's residence, not the Jiang family's back garden!"
The words had barely left his mouth when another heavy bout of coughing sounded from within. Nanny Zhou spun around and took two steps toward the courtyard, only to stumble.
This time, even the guard at the gate turned to look.
The steward muttered a curse. "Only a few days after the wedding festivities, and now we have this ill-omened business."

At last I saw an opening. "If you're worried about letting a doctor inside, you could bring the patient to the gate instead. The doctor won't touch your account books or see the masters. He'll only examine the patient. You can have someone watch the whole time if you like."
He gave me a cold stare.

I hurried on. "The Jiang family will cover the consultation and medicine for now. You can decide who owes what afterward. And if he gets any worse, you'll have one fewer person helping in the rear kitchen and will have to find a replacement."
After a long silence, the steward finally waved a hand.
"Let the doctor in. He may examine the patient in the gatehouse and nowhere else. None of you are to follow him."
Delighted, I was just about to speak when Chuntao pinched me again.
I shut my mouth at once.
Once Doctor Fang had gone through the gate, we waited outside for what felt like ages.
The sun climbed higher, and water from the vegetable baskets seeped across the ground. I'd nervously picked almost all the mud off the radishes by the time Doctor Fang came out.
He looked grim.

"This has gone on too long," he told the steward. "There's a great deal of phlegm and heat in his chest, and he's struggling to breathe. I can't tell you exactly what's wrong from a quick examination here. He needs to be seen properly at a clinic. If the breathlessness gets worse or he becomes confused again, don't delay."
The steward was plainly reluctant. "Can't he be treated inside the residence?"
"Medicine can be brought in, but his condition may not wait. If he cannot be moved, call the household's regular doctor for another examination. If he can, it's best to take him out today."
I immediately looked toward Nanny Zhou.
She stood behind the gate, head lowered, one hand gripping the edge of her sleeve.

The steward hesitated for a long time before saying, "Very well. I'll have a sedan chair prepared and take him to the clinic in the west of town. Old Zhou, you may go along to look after him. If all goes well, come back this afternoon."
I almost cheered.
But Nanny Zhou looked up at me, and something in her eyes made me swallow the words.
She was terrified of going too far.

Her whole life was still inside that gate: the wages she'd earned over more than a decade, her husband's medicine, the occasional letters from her son. If she went out today, she couldn't know whether she'd be allowed back tomorrow.
Nanny Zhou didn't ask me to save her. She only bowed to the steward. "Thank you, sir."
Then she helped her husband into the sedan chair and went with the Xie household's people toward the western clinic.
They hadn't escaped.
The household had finally agreed to let a sick man receive medical care. That was all.
I was about to follow them in secret, but Wen Li emerged from the pharmacy and shook her head.
"There are people accompanying the sedan chair," she said. "If you follow now, you'll only draw suspicion onto her."
I stood there for a long moment.
"So after all that work, all we achieved was getting a sick man seen by a doctor?"
Wen Li glanced toward the clinic.
"That's still a good thing."
I knew she was right, but it still left a bitter taste in my mouth.
Saving people wasn't nearly as satisfying as it looked in the books.
Some were still being watched. Others still had to go back. We didn't even dare say, "Come with me."
That afternoon, A-Qin was waiting at Wen Li's old house when a clinic attendant brought something from Nanny Zhou.
It wasn't a key. And it wasn't an account book.
It was a piece of cloth lining removed from an old medicine pouch. A tiny slip of paper had been stitched to it, with three short lines written on it:
The old Du family mill, western outskirts. Ninth day of the twelfth lunar month, three years ago. Original lease register, Volume B, Entry Seven.
"Where did this come from?" I asked.

A-Qin shook her head. "She only said she'd once handled an old lease as well, and that the date in the accounts hadn't looked right. She didn't dare take the original register, so she copied down this reference."
Wen Li held the slip, her fingers slowly tightening around it.
"My father's report from that year mentioned the Du family."
"So the grain went to the mill?" I asked.
"We don't know." She smoothed the paper flat. "It might only mean the mill's lease changed hands that day. We need to check the original register before drawing any conclusions from three lines."
By now, I was getting used to hearing that.
We took the slip to Gu Huaichuan. The moment he saw "B Seven," he pulled an old index of lease registrations from his desk to check it.

"There was indeed a Du family mill in the western outskirts," he said. "But this is a copy of a copy. It doesn't prove any grain was delivered there. I'll find out who holds the original lease register and check the list of people who handled the tenancy at the time."
"Can we go and take a look first?" I asked.
"You may look from the public road."
"What about inside the yard?"
"No."
"Just one quick look?"
Gu Huaichuan finally raised his head.

"Miss Jiang, last time you said you only wanted to borrow a boat ticket. You ended up bringing me two shopkeepers and a private ledger. I suggest you stop treating the words 'just one quick look' as though they were harmless."
Wen Li pressed her lips together, struggling not to laugh.

Gu Huaichuan filed the slip separately, recorded the names of those who had passed on the lead, along with the time and its source, and only then said, "You've both been a great help today. Leave the rest to me."
Once we left the Ministry of Punishments, I let out a long breath.
"For once, Lord Gu didn't accuse me of getting in the way."
"He just doesn't want you getting in the way again," Wen Li said.
"Is there a difference?"
"Yes. Now he knows to stop you before you start."
I was about to argue when someone called Wen Li's name from the street corner.
It was A-Qin.
She was out of breath, clutching a prescription she'd brought from the clinic.

"Miss Wen, Auntie Yuan just came out through the household's purchasing gate and asked me to pass on a message. When Nanny Zhou returned today, she overheard the steward saying they were moving that batch of old boxes from the mill tonight."
Wen Li and I both stopped dead.
"Old boxes?" I repeated.
"She couldn't hear what was inside," A-Qin said. "Only that everything had to be loaded before the third watch of the night."
Wen Li immediately turned toward the Ministry's entrance.
"Tell Lord Gu first."
I ran back with her.
But as we reached the steps, another thought suddenly struck me.
Xie Linzhou had allowed Nanny Zhou's husband to leave the residence for treatment. He also knew someone had arranged for a doctor.
If he found out who had delivered medicine to the back lane today, would that lead him straight to Nanny Zhou?
We hadn't succeeded in smuggling anyone out.
But we might well have put her in greater danger than she'd been in yesterday.
translations: 我第一次发现，救人也分许多种。
比如我说“把人藏进菜车”，温梨说“不行”。
我说“那就假扮官差”，秦叔说“不行”。
我再说“给门房塞钱”，我娘干脆把算盘推过来。
“你先算算，行贿败露以后，姜记还剩几间铺子。”
我只好把算盘推回去。
“娘，那总不能看着他们在侯府里挨饿吧？”
“你不是要送药么？”她说，“送药就正经送药。人家肯不肯收，你先去问。别一见门就想着钻。”
秦叔在旁边点头：“姜家每天给侯府后厨送菜，走的是供货账。后厨签收了，才算送到。菜车可以送到后巷，车夫不能想进哪个院就进哪个院。”
温梨又补一句：“周嬷嬷的丈夫病着，真要搬人，也得先让大夫看看能不能动。”
我望着桌边三个人，深深觉得自己穿错书了。
别人家的恶毒女配穿书，今天智斗反派，明天执掌后宫。
我穿书，想救个人，先被迫参加了三堂风险评估。
不过，该准备的还是准备了。
秦叔替我们请来一位在城西坐堂的方大夫。阿芹回话说，冯叔烧得神志不清，咳嗽得厉害，周嬷嬷盼着能请大夫进府看看，并不愿现在就丢下丈夫独自逃走。
这一回，我至少知道她自己想要什么了。
次日清晨，后巷的风又湿又冷。
我套着粗布围裙，和春桃坐在送菜车上。温梨留在隔壁药铺等消息，秦叔陪着方大夫守在巷口。我们原本只想先把药送进去，看看后院有没有见人的机会。
守门亲卫照例拦车。
“今日的菜放门外，别往里送。”
掌车的伙计愣住：“以前都是送到厨房验重，放这里叫谁签收？”
“里面有人来搬。”
“那少了两筐萝卜算谁的？”我掀开车帘，“算您的吗？”
亲卫上下看我两眼：“你又是谁？”
“姜家管账的。”
他看着我身上的围裙，显然不信。
“管账的亲自送菜？”
“账房封了，家里人手不够。您不让进我也不硬闯，可货得点清楚。不然回头您府上的厨房说我们缺斤短两，我拿什么跟我娘交代？”
我刚说完，门里就走出个圆脸管事，脸色比锅底还黑。
“姜家的货我们照收，少在门口嚷。谢府哪日短过你们银子？”
“上个月十三车蔬菜，账上还有两车没结。”秦叔提前让我背过，我答得飞快，“要不您顺手把那两车也结了？”
管事被噎住了。
春桃悄悄在我胳膊上掐了一下，示意我见好就收。
就在这时，院里忽然传来一阵咳嗽声。声音隔着墙都听得出来，像有什么堵在胸口。
我看到一个头发花白的妇人推着小木车走过门洞，肩上披一件旧褐衣。她没有往我们这边看，只停下来，弯腰去捡地上的药包。
亲卫喝道：“周嬷嬷，谁准你来这里？”
她慢慢站直。
“是厨房叫我送旧筐。”
“旧筐不劳你。”
周嬷嬷把手放在车辕上，指节凸得厉害。我忽然想起温梨说的那句话——她没想做英雄，只想让家里人平平安安。
我本来准备好的三十句胡搅蛮缠，一句也说不出来了。
春桃从菜筐底下拿出一个小药包，是方大夫按阿芹说的病状先备的普通退热药材，外头写了“需面诊，勿擅服”。
“嬷嬷，”她轻声说，“有人托我们带给您。”
周嬷嬷没有伸手。她先看了一眼管事，又看向我们。
“侯府不缺药。”管事说。
“那就更好。”我接过话，“我们请的大夫就在巷口。病人都咳成这样了，麻烦您让大夫看一眼。若真不缺药，我们也好回去交差。”
管事脸色变了：“谁让你请大夫的？”
“没谁。”我说，“是卖菜的人多管闲事。”
“这里是侯府，不是你们姜记的后院！”
他话音刚落，里头又传来一阵沉闷的咳嗽。周嬷嬷猛地转身，往院内走了两步，脚下却一个踉跄。
这回连门口的亲卫都看了过去。
管事低声骂了一句：“大喜过后没几天，偏出这种晦气事。”
我终于抓住一点机会：“您要是怕大夫进府，那让病人抬到门口也行。大夫不碰账、不见主人，只看病。您若不放心，派人在旁边盯着。”
他冷着脸看我。
我赶紧补充：“诊钱、药钱都由姜家垫，之后您愿意算谁的再算。人要真病坏了，后厨缺个人，您还得重新找。”
半晌，管事终于挥手。
“叫大夫进来，只许在门房看诊。你们谁也不准跟。”
我一喜，刚想说话，春桃又掐了我一下。
我立即闭嘴。
方大夫进门以后，我们在外头等了很久。
日头渐高，菜筐边的水渗了一地。我紧张得把萝卜上的泥抠得快干净了，才看见方大夫出来。
他脸色不好。
“这病人拖得太久，胸中痰热重，呼吸也费力。”他对管事说，“我不敢只凭这里看一眼就断是什么病。得送去医馆继续看，若再发喘或神志不清，不能耽误。”
管事明显不愿意：“侯府里不能治？”
“药可以送进去，病情却未必等得。人若搬不了，就请府里常用的大夫再诊；若能搬，最好今日送出去。”
我立刻看向周嬷嬷。
她站在门后，低着头，一只手还紧紧捏着衣角。
管事犹豫了许久，终于说：“既如此，我叫人备轿，送到城西医馆。周婆子，你也跟去照应。午后无事就回来。”
我差点欢呼出声。
可周嬷嬷抬头看了我一眼，那眼神让我把话咽回去了。
她根本不敢走远。
她的家还在侯府，过去十几年挣来的月钱、丈夫用的药、儿子偶尔寄回来的信，全压在这道门里。今日出了门，明日能不能回来，都不知道。
周嬷嬷没有向我求救，只对管事行礼：“多谢管事。”
随后她扶着丈夫上了轿，跟着侯府的人往城西去。
这不是逃出来了。
是府里终于肯把病人送去看诊。
我本想偷偷跟过去，温梨却从药铺出来，冲我摇了摇头。
“有人跟轿子，”她说，“你现在跟着，只会叫人怀疑她。”
我在原地站了好一会儿。
“那我们忙了半天，就只让人看了个病？”
温梨看了看医馆的方向。
“这也很好。”
我知道她说得对，可心里还是有点不是滋味。
救人的结果没有书里那么痛快。
有人依旧被盯着，有人依旧要回去。我们连一句“跟我走”都不敢说。
午后，阿芹在温梨的旧宅等到了周嬷嬷托医馆伙计送出的东西。
不是钥匙，也不是账册。
是一块拆下来的布衬，原本缝在旧药囊里面。上头用针脚固定着一张小纸，记了三行字：
西郊杜记旧磨坊。三年前腊月初九。租契原簿乙七。
“这是哪里来的？”我问。
阿芹摇头：“她只说，自己还经手过一份旧契，见到账上的日期觉得不对。她没敢把原簿带走，只抄了这行。”
温梨握着纸，手指一点点收紧。
“我爹当年的呈报里提过杜记。”
“所以粮去了磨坊？”我问。
“不知道。”她把纸摊平，“可能只是那天磨坊租契有变更。得先查原簿，不能拿这几行字当结论。”
这话我竟然已经听习惯了。
我们拿着纸去见顾怀川。他看到“乙七”，立刻从案头抽出一份旧契登记目录核对。
“西郊确有杜记磨坊。”他说，“但你们这份是转抄，不能证明粮到了那里。我会查存契的人，核对当年租佃的经手名册。”
“我们可以先去看看吗？”我问。
“可以在官道上看。”
“院子里呢？”
“不可以。”
“只看一眼呢？”
顾怀川终于抬起头。
“姜姑娘，上回你说只借一张船票，结果带来了两位掌柜和一本私账。这次我劝你别把‘只看一眼’四个字说得太轻巧。”
温梨抿住嘴，忍了半天才没笑出来。
顾怀川把纸收进单独的卷夹，留下我们转交线索的名字、时间和来处，才说：“你们今日已经帮了大忙。剩下的交给我。”
出了刑部，我长舒一口气。
“难得顾大人没说我添乱。”
“他只是不想再让你添乱。”温梨说。
“有区别吗？”
“有。他现在知道要提前拦你了。”
我正要反驳，街口忽然有人叫了温梨一声。
是阿芹。
她跑得气喘吁吁，手里攥着一张从医馆带回的药方。
“温姑娘，刚才袁婶从侯府采买门出来，托我带句话。周嬷嬷今日回去时，听见管事在议论，今夜要把磨坊那批旧箱子挪走。”
我和温梨同时停住。
“旧箱子？”我问。
“她没听见里面是什么。”阿芹说，“只听见‘三更之前，必须装完’。”
温梨立刻回身望向刑部门口。
“先告诉顾大人。”
我跟着她往回跑。
走到台阶前，我却突然想起另一个问题。
谢临舟把周嬷嬷的丈夫送出府了，也知道有人替她找了大夫。
他若查到今日是谁去后巷送的药，会不会顺着摸到周嬷嬷身上？
这次我们没有成功偷出一个人。
但很可能，已经让她比昨天更危险了。

annotations.explain: It was the first time 后面常用过去完成时来强调此前从未有过的体验；这里叙述者回顾当时的新认识。
annotations.example: It was the first time I had spoken in public.

annotations.explain: there are different ways to do something 是谈论解决途径的常见结构，ways 后可接 to do。
annotations.example: There are different ways to solve this problem.

annotations.explain: 用于引出具体例子，比 for example 略有书面感，但口语也常用。
annotations.example: Some tasks can be shared; for instance, we can divide the research.

annotations.explain: hide somebody in a place 表示把人藏于某处；注意 in 后接藏身地点。
annotations.example: They hid the documents in a wooden box.

annotations.explain: dress up as somebody 表示穿上服装假扮某种身份，不等于日常穿得体面。
annotations.example: He dressed up as a doctor for the play.

annotations.explain: suggest doing something 是常用结构；suggest 后不能直接接 to do 表示建议。
annotations.example: She suggested taking a different route.

annotations.explain: push something across the table 用动作代替直接回应；across 表示横越桌面到另一侧。
annotations.example: He pushed the contract across the desk.

annotations.explain: work out 表示计算、想清楚；后面可直接接 how many/how much 等间接疑问句。
annotations.example: Can you work out how much we owe?

annotations.explain: 条件句用 would have left 表示假设后仍会保有的数量，left 是补语。
annotations.example: How much money would we have left?

annotations.explain: come to light 是固定表达，指隐情、事实等最终被揭露。
annotations.example: The fraud came to light years later.

annotations.explain: quietly 作方式副词，搭配动作可传递服软或无奈，而无需解释心理。
annotations.example: She quietly closed the door.

annotations.explain: stand by 既可指待命，也可指眼看事情发生而不行动；此处依据语境取后者。
annotations.example: We couldn't just stand by and do nothing.

annotations.explain: leave someone to do something 表示放任或让某人处于某境地；被动为 be left to。
annotations.example: The villagers were left to fend for themselves.

annotations.explain: be supposed to 表示按计划、责任或常理应做某事；反问形式带提醒意味。
annotations.example: Aren't you supposed to be at work?

annotations.explain: deliver 可以送货、信件或药品；deliver medicine 不等于 administer medicine（给病人用药）。
annotations.example: The pharmacy delivers medicine to elderly patients.

annotations.explain: ask whether 后是间接问句，用陈述语序，适合表达先征询意愿。
annotations.example: Ask whether they can come tomorrow.

annotations.explain: sneak 表示悄悄移动、潜行；through 强调穿过入口或通道。
annotations.example: The cat sneaked through the open door.

annotations.explain: go on the books 在此表示登记在账簿上；不是字面的去到书本上。
annotations.example: Every purchase must go on the books.

annotations.explain: count as + 形容词或名词，表示被认定为某状态；商业上未签收不一定算交付。
annotations.example: The package only counts as delivered after signing.

annotations.explain: sign for something 是签字确认收到，而 sign something 可以泛指签署任何文件。
annotations.example: Please sign for the parcel.

annotations.explain: wander into 强调未按明确路线随意走入，语气比 enter 更松散。
annotations.example: A tourist wandered into the private courtyard.

annotations.explain: whichever 可作限定词，表示任意一个符合条件的选择；带有不受限制之意。
annotations.example: Choose whichever seat you like.

annotations.explain: even if 引导让步假设，与 even though（尽管事实如此）有所区别。
annotations.example: Even if it rains, we'll go.

annotations.explain: fit to do 或 fit to be done 表示身体或条件适合某事，常用于是否安全的判断。
annotations.example: He wasn't fit to travel.

annotations.explain: have the distinct feeling that... 用于表达清晰但主观的预感。
annotations.example: I had the distinct feeling we were being followed.

annotations.explain: transmigrate 本义是灵魂转移；在穿书题材中用作进入另一个世界的设定词。
annotations.example: She transmigrated into a historical novel.

annotations.explain: outsmart somebody 指靠机智胜过某人，不一定通过武力。
annotations.example: The detective outsmarted the thief.

annotations.explain: take charge of 常指承担管理职责；与 be in charge of 的状态表达区分。
annotations.example: She took charge of the family business.

annotations.explain: end up doing 表示最终落得某结果；sit through 指耐着性子听完冗长活动。
annotations.example: We ended up sitting through a three-hour lecture.

annotations.explain: 常见工作场景名词搭配，这里故意把现代管理用语放进古风故事制造反差。
annotations.example: The team carried out a risk assessment.

annotations.explain: have preparations to make 表示尚有准备工作，to make 作后置定语。
annotations.example: We still have arrangements to make.

annotations.explain: see patients 是医生看诊的固定搭配，see 不是简单的用眼睛看。
annotations.example: The doctor sees patients on weekdays.

annotations.explain: send word (that...) 是托人传话的固定表达。
annotations.example: She sent word that she would arrive late.

annotations.explain: be aware of 表示知道、意识到；barely 强调程度接近零。
annotations.example: He was barely aware of the noise.

annotations.explain: with 引出伴随身体症状，不能将 with 一概译为使用。
annotations.example: She arrived with a bad cough.

annotations.explain: examine 在医疗语境中是检查病情，语气比 look at 更专业。
annotations.example: A doctor examined the patient.

annotations.explain: have no intention of doing 是常用固定结构，of 后接动名词。
annotations.example: I have no intention of leaving early.

annotations.explain: abandon 比 leave 更强调遗弃、抛弃的责任意味。
annotations.example: He refused to abandon his friends.

annotations.explain: 强调当事人的意愿与主体性，不等同于替她决定。
annotations.example: She needed to make that choice for herself.

annotations.explain: 时间衔接表达，常在叙事段首交代时间推进。
annotations.example: The next morning, the town was quiet.

annotations.explain: coarse 描述材质粗糙；compound modifier 用连字符构成前置定语。
annotations.example: He wore a coarse-cloth jacket.

annotations.explain: wait at 强调等候地点；pharmacy 是药房，不必然是现代药店。
annotations.example: I'll wait at the pharmacy for you.

annotations.explain: wait for news 是常用搭配，news 为不可数名词。
annotations.example: We waited for news all afternoon.

annotations.phrase: at the mouth of the lane
annotations.explain: mouth 可比喻河口、洞口、巷口等开口处。
annotations.example: A guard stood at the mouth of the alley.

annotations.explain: all... meant to do was... 强调目的有限；mean to do 表示打算。
annotations.example: All I meant to do was help.

annotations.explain: a chance to do something 常用于表达机会，speak to 强调交谈对象。
annotations.example: I finally had a chance to speak to her.

annotations.explain: 作为句首话语标记，说明事情与平常相同。
annotations.example: As usual, the train was crowded.

annotations.explain: stop somebody/something 表示使其停下，也常指检查时拦停车辆。
annotations.example: The officer stopped the car.

annotations.explain: leave + 宾语 + 地点副词，表示让物品留在某处。
annotations.example: Please leave your shoes outside.

annotations.explain: take something in 在这里指把货送进场所，语境不同可指理解、收留。
annotations.example: They wouldn't let us take the bags in.

annotations.explain: weigh 作及物动词表示给某物称重量；被动 be weighed。
annotations.example: All goods must be weighed.

annotations.explain: sign for something 是签字确认收货；这是本章供货争议的核心表达。
annotations.example: The receptionist signed for the delivery.

annotations.explain: come and do 在口语中表示来做某事；collect 是领取、取走。
annotations.example: Can you come and collect the parcel?

annotations.explain: go missing 表示失踪或遗失，不意味着已证明有人偷窃。
annotations.example: Two files went missing.

annotations.explain: whose 表所有格，疑问的是责任或账目归属。
annotations.example: Whose account should this charge go on?

annotations.explain: look somebody up and down 是从头到脚打量的固定表达，常含审视意味。
annotations.example: The interviewer looked me up and down.

annotations.explain: keep the accounts 意为做账、管账；keep 并非保存的单一含义。
annotations.example: She keeps the company's accounts.

annotations.phrase: didn't believe a word of it
annotations.explain: not believe a word of it 是较口语化的强烈否定。
annotations.example: He told me a story, but I didn't believe a word of it.

annotations.explain: short-handed 是常见经营/职场形容词，与 short of hands 意思接近。
annotations.example: We're short-handed this morning.

annotations.explain: force one's way + 方向 表示强行挤入或进入，不等于正常出入。
annotations.example: The crowd forced its way through the gate.

annotations.explain: be short on something 表示不足，买卖货物时可描述缺斤短两。
annotations.example: The shipment was short on weight.

annotations.explain: how am I supposed to... 是常见反问，表示现实困难或不满，不一定真在询问方法。
annotations.example: How am I supposed to finish this alone?

annotations.explain: barely + 过去完成时与 when/后续事件呼应，强调两件事接连发生。
annotations.example: I'd barely sat down when the phone rang.

annotations.explain: emerge from 表示从遮蔽处出现，常用于叙事。
annotations.example: A figure emerged from the shadows.

annotations.explain: 比较级 than 加夸张意象，描写脸色阴沉，不是字面颜色测量。
annotations.example: His expression was darker than a storm cloud.

annotations.phrase: accept the Jiang family's goods as usual
annotations.explain: as usual 修饰动作方式，意味着没有改变惯例。
annotations.example: We will accept orders as usual.

annotations.explain: make a scene 是固定表达，指在公共场合大吵大闹。
annotations.example: Please don't make a scene.

annotations.explain: shortchange 字面是找零钱不足，也可泛指欠付或不公平对待。
annotations.example: The customer complained that he'd been shortchanged.

annotations.explain: cartload 是装满一车的量；load 可与车/卡车组成计量复合词。
annotations.example: They delivered three cartloads of grain.

annotations.explain: unpaid 用于账款表示未支付，不能自动推断买方拒绝付款的原因。
annotations.example: Several invoices are still unpaid.

annotations.explain: since 可以引导原因状语从句，口语中用来顺势提出要求。
annotations.example: Since you're here, could you help me?

annotations.explain: settle a bill/debt/invoice 指结清欠款，不是安置或平息。
annotations.example: We should settle the bill today.

annotations.explain: be lost for words 是因惊讶、窘迫等说不出话的固定表达。
annotations.example: She was lost for words.

annotations.explain: discreet 表示谨慎不引人注意，区别 discrete（分离的）。
annotations.example: He gave me a discreet signal.

annotations.explain: push one's luck 指在已有好运或宽容下继续冒险索取。
annotations.example: Don't push your luck.

annotations.explain: 用于引入与前一句同时或突然发生的新事件。
annotations.example: Just then, the door opened.

annotations.explain: a fit of coughing 是症状发作的一阵，fit of + 名词还可搭配 laughter。
annotations.example: A fit of coughing interrupted him.

annotations.explain: be lodged in 指物体卡住或嵌在某处，这里是对咳嗽的比喻。
annotations.example: The splinter was lodged in his finger.

annotations.explain: drape something over 强调松松搭着、覆盖在表面。
annotations.example: She draped a shawl over her shoulders.

annotations.explain: look someone's way 指朝某人所在方向看，是叙事中常用口语搭配。
annotations.example: He didn't even look my way.

annotations.explain: bend to do 表示俯身做事；retrieve 强调取回或拾回。
annotations.example: She bent to retrieve her keys.

annotations.explain: bark 作言语动词时表示粗声、厉声说话，塑造命令语气。
annotations.example: "Out!" the guard barked.

annotations.explain: permission to do something 是常见搭配；permission 通常不可数。
annotations.example: You need permission to enter.

annotations.explain: straighten up 表示把身体挺直，也可以指整理整齐。
annotations.example: He straightened up when the teacher came in.

annotations.explain: bring back 表示带回原处、归还，也可表示勾起记忆。
annotations.example: Please bring back the tools.

annotations.explain: rest something on 表示轻放或搁在表面，常用于动作描写。
annotations.example: She rested her hand on the railing.

annotations.explain: stand out 不只指显眼，也可描述身体轮廓突出。
annotations.example: The veins stood out on his hands.

annotations.explain: set out to do 表示带着目标着手做，常用否定对照实际经历。
annotations.example: We didn't set out to become famous.

annotations.explain: not one of + 复数名词，强调完全否定，后常接单数动词。
annotations.example: Not one of them agreed.

annotations.explain: come out 此处指话语说出来，其他语境可指出版、出现等。
annotations.example: The words wouldn't come out.

annotations.explain: beneath 是介词，较 below 更常带紧贴覆盖关系。
annotations.example: She pulled the letter from beneath a book.

annotations.explain: based on 引出信息依据，不表示结论一定正确。
annotations.example: The estimate is based on last year's sales.

annotations.explain: seek 在正式语境表示寻求；与 medical examination 搭配。
annotations.example: Patients should seek an examination promptly.

annotations.explain: without + 名词 突出缺乏必要条件；此处是药包的明确限制。
annotations.example: Don't change the dosage without medical advice.

annotations.explain: reach for 表示伸手够取；与 reach out to（联系某人）不同。
annotations.example: She reached for her bag.

annotations.explain: all the better 表示前述情况反而使事情更有利。
annotations.example: If you're free tomorrow, all the better.

annotations.explain: at the end of 指地点末端，别和 in the end（最终）混淆。
annotations.example: He waited at the end of the street.

annotations.explain: take a look 是口语固定搭配，后常用 at 引出对象。
annotations.example: Could you take a look at this?

annotations.explain: 用于引出最低程度的肯定或安慰，不等于最多。
annotations.example: At least we tried.

annotations.explain: one's face changes 描写突然的情绪反应，常带惊讶或紧张。
annotations.example: Her face changed when she heard the news.

annotations.explain: stick one's nose where it doesn't belong 是指管不该管的事的口语表达。
annotations.example: Stop sticking your nose into my business.

annotations.explain: back garden 本义是后院花园，此处用来对比两处宅院的管理边界。
annotations.example: The children played in the back garden.

annotations.explain: only to do 常表示出乎意料、反而不如愿的结果。
annotations.example: He hurried home, only to find the door locked.

annotations.explain: turn to do 表示转身去做动作，区别 turn to somebody for help。
annotations.example: She turned to look at the window.

annotations.explain: mutter 表示含糊低声说；curse 可作名词指骂人的话。
annotations.example: He muttered a curse under his breath.

annotations.explain: at last 强调经过等待或努力后终于发生，比 finally 更突出情绪。
annotations.example: At last, the letter arrived.

annotations.explain: see an opening 是发现突破口或可利用的时机，常见于谈判叙述。
annotations.example: She saw an opening and asked another question.

annotations.explain: be worried about doing 表示担忧做某事；about 后用动名词。
annotations.example: They're worried about losing customers.

annotations.explain: instead 可置于句末表示换一种做法，与 instead of + 名词/动名词区分。
annotations.example: We stayed home instead.

annotations.explain: the whole time 是自然的口语时间状语，表示从头到尾。
annotations.example: I was nervous the whole time.

annotations.explain: give somebody a stare 是用名词化动作描写神态，cold 修饰目光态度。
annotations.example: She gave him a puzzled look.

annotations.explain: hurry on 可表示匆匆继续说话或行动，体现怕被打断。
annotations.example: He hurried on before she could object.

annotations.explain: cover a cost/bill 表示支付、负担费用，非遮盖。
annotations.example: Insurance may cover the consultation.

annotations.explain: for now 强调现阶段安排未必长期如此。
annotations.example: We'll keep the plan for now.

annotations.explain: 间接疑问结构，what 是 owed 的内容，常见于账目争议。
annotations.example: Let's work out who owes what.

annotations.explain: get + 比较级表示状态变化，worse 比 bad 程度更严重。
annotations.example: Call me if the pain gets any worse.

annotations.explain: one fewer + 可数名词；与 less 用于不可数概念的常见区别。
annotations.example: We have one fewer volunteer today.

annotations.explain: 用于叙事节奏转换，表现决定艰难或气氛紧张。
annotations.example: After a long silence, she answered.

annotations.explain: nowhere else 是地点的排他性表达。
annotations.example: Keep this file here and nowhere else.

annotations.explain: none of you 强调多人中的全部否定，后可接 are。
annotations.example: None of you are allowed inside.

annotations.explain: be about to do 表示动作即将发生，常与 when 引入打断事件。
annotations.example: I was just about to leave when she called.

annotations.explain: at once 在此表示马上；也可表示同时，需看上下文。
annotations.example: Come here at once.

annotations.explain: what felt like ages 是主观时间夸张描写，不是精确计时。
annotations.example: We waited for what felt like hours.

annotations.explain: seep 强调液体缓慢渗出，across 表示扩散的方向或范围。
annotations.example: Water seeped across the floor.

annotations.explain: by the time 引导时间从句，常与完成时组合说明截止某时已发生的事。
annotations.example: By the time we arrived, the shop had closed.

annotations.explain: look + 形容词描写外观，grim 常表示严肃、不乐观。
annotations.example: The doctor looked grim.

annotations.explain: go on 表示持续；too long 带有超出合理范围的评价。
annotations.example: The dispute had gone on too long.

annotations.explain: struggle to do 表示艰难地完成某动作；描写症状但不自动给出诊断。
annotations.example: He was struggling to breathe after the race.

annotations.explain: can't tell exactly 在此承认信息不足，符合医生不作武断诊断的语气。
annotations.example: I can't tell exactly what caused it.

annotations.explain: from 引出判断依据，强调证据有限。
annotations.example: You can't know everything from a quick examination.

annotations.meaning: 到医馆接受进一步检查
annotations.explain: be seen 是医生接诊的被动说法，properly 强调充分、妥善。
annotations.example: She needs to be seen by a specialist.

annotations.explain: become + 形容词强调状态变化，confused 在医疗情境中可指意识混乱。
annotations.example: He became confused after the fever.

annotations.explain: reluctant to do 表示不愿做，plainly 是明显地。
annotations.example: She was plainly reluctant to agree.

annotations.explain: may 表不确定性，not wait 是将病情拟人化地表达紧迫。
annotations.example: This decision may not wait until morning.

annotations.explain: 条件从句中的被动语态，把焦点放在病人的身体限制上。
annotations.example: If the patient cannot be moved, call for help.

annotations.explain: regular 可指固定、经常使用的人员或服务，非仅指规律。
annotations.example: Ask your regular doctor for advice.

annotations.explain: It's best to do 表建议，语气较 should 柔和。
annotations.example: It's best to check the details first.

annotations.explain: grip 表紧握，常用于强调紧张情绪。
annotations.example: He was gripping the edge of the table.

annotations.explain: hesitate 表犹豫，后可接 before doing。
annotations.example: She hesitated before answering.

annotations.explain: have something done 是使役结构，表示安排他人完成某事。
annotations.example: I'll have the room cleaned tomorrow.

annotations.explain: go along 表示同行，也可表示同意，需看语境。
annotations.example: Can I go along with you?

annotations.explain: 固定条件表达，常用于未确定的未来安排。
annotations.example: If all goes well, we'll finish by Friday.

annotations.explain: almost + 动词表示差一点做出某动作，但通常没有真正发生。
annotations.example: I almost laughed out loud.

annotations.explain: swallow one's words 比喻忍住没说出口，生动表达克制。
annotations.example: He swallowed the angry words.

annotations.explain: be terrified of + 名词/动名词，程度强于 afraid of。
annotations.example: She was terrified of leaving home.

annotations.explain: occasional 放在名词前表示间或发生而非常态。
annotations.example: I enjoy the occasional day off.

annotations.explain: be allowed back 表获准返回，区别成功返回本身。
annotations.example: They weren't allowed back into the building.

annotations.explain: ask somebody to do something 是请求他人做某事的常用句型。
annotations.example: He asked me to help.

annotations.explain: go with 在此是陪同，并不代表赞同。
annotations.example: She went with her father to the clinic.

annotations.explain: 句子独立出现可收束或纠正上一事件被过度解读的意义。
annotations.example: We had confirmed the date. That was all.

annotations.explain: in secret 表示秘密地做某事；与 secretly 语义相近。
annotations.example: They met in secret.

annotations.explain: draw suspicion on/onto somebody 指使人受到怀疑，说明跟随会增加风险。
annotations.example: That behavior could draw suspicion onto her.

annotations.explain: moment 通常是短暂时刻，a long moment 用叙事夸张突出停顿。
annotations.example: For a long moment, nobody spoke.

annotations.explain: after all that... 强调付出与结果之间的落差。
annotations.example: After all that effort, we still failed.

annotations.explain: still 强调即便存在局限也认可某一积极结果。
annotations.example: It didn't work perfectly, but that's still a good thing.

annotations.phrase: left a bitter taste in my mouth
annotations.explain: leave a bitter taste in one's mouth 是指经历让人不快的固定表达。
annotations.example: The unfair decision left a bitter taste in my mouth.

annotations.explain: not nearly as + 形容词 + as 表程度显著不及。
annotations.example: It wasn't nearly as easy as I expected.

annotations.explain: 进行时被动 be being watched 表持续正在受到监视。
annotations.example: They suspected they were still being watched.

annotations.explain: not even dare to do 强调行为界限与恐惧。
annotations.example: He didn't even dare to ask.

annotations.phrase: waiting at Wen Li's old house
annotations.explain: wait at 某地点表示在那里等候；地点介词不能遗漏。
annotations.example: She was waiting at the station.

annotations.explain: bring something from somewhere 清楚标记物品来源。
annotations.example: He brought a note from the office.

annotations.explain: remove something from 指将物件从原附着处取下。
annotations.example: She removed the label from the bottle.

annotations.explain: stitch something to something 表示缝到某物表面。
annotations.example: A tag was stitched to the bag.

annotations.explain: written on 是过去分词后置定语，修饰前面的文本或物件。
annotations.example: There was a number written on it.

annotations.explain: 问句固定口语表达，可询问物件来源或想法出处。
annotations.example: Where did this idea come from?

annotations.explain: look right 表示看起来正确、妥当；否定 often 暗示疑点未证实。
annotations.example: The figures didn't look right.

annotations.explain: dare 作实义动词时可接 to do 或省略 to 的变体，口语常见 didn't dare do。
annotations.example: I didn't dare tell her.

annotations.explain: copy down 表示把听到或看到的内容写下，常作为记录动作。
annotations.example: Copy down the address.

annotations.explain: 独立结构/描写性分词强调同时发生的情绪反应。
annotations.example: She waited, her hands trembling.

annotations.explain: mention + 宾语，不必再加 about；错误形式 mention about。
annotations.example: He mentioned the meeting yesterday.

annotations.explain: change hands 是产权或控制权转移的固定表达。
annotations.example: The shop changed hands twice.

annotations.explain: draw a conclusion 是固定搭配，before 后用动名词。
annotations.example: Check the evidence before drawing conclusions.

annotations.explain: get used to + 名词/动名词；to 是介词，不是不定式标记。
annotations.example: I'm getting used to working late.

annotations.explain: the moment 可作连词，引导时间从句，语义接近 as soon as。
annotations.example: The moment she arrived, we started.

annotations.explain: pull something from 强调手部快速取出。
annotations.example: He pulled a folder from the drawer.

annotations.explain: indeed 用于确认事实，但只确认说话人所核实的范围。
annotations.example: The record did indeed exist.

annotations.explain: a copy of a copy 突出文书已多次转写，证据效力可能需要进一步核验。
annotations.example: This document is only a copy of a copy.

annotations.explain: prove 常接从句或宾语，区别 suggest（提示可能性）。
annotations.example: One clue doesn't prove the claim.

annotations.explain: find out 后接间接疑问句，保持陈述语序。
annotations.example: We need to find out who signed it.

annotations.explain: 用于限定历史背景，区别 on time（准时）。
annotations.example: She worked there at the time.

annotations.explain: take a look 是口语高频表达，first 表先后步骤。
annotations.example: Can we take a look first?

annotations.explain: public 描述公众可通行的区域，与私人院落对照。
annotations.example: Visitors must stay on the public road.

annotations.explain: what about + 名词/动名词 用来追问另一个选项。
annotations.example: What about tomorrow morning?

annotations.explain: just 和 quick 叠加强调要求很小，常是请求对方放宽限制的策略。
annotations.example: Just one quick look, please.

annotations.explain: end up doing 表示结果与最初计划不同。
annotations.example: I ended up bringing three friends.

annotations.explain: suggest (that) + 句子可省略 that，后接陈述内容；stop doing 表示停止原行为。
annotations.example: I suggest you stop arguing.

annotations.explain: as though 引导方式或假设从句，常用来表达评价和反讽。
annotations.example: He acted as though nothing had happened.

annotations.explain: press one's lips together 是控制表情的常见动作描写。
annotations.example: She pressed her lips together to keep from smiling.

annotations.explain: struggle not to do 表示努力克制；否定不定式放在 to 前。
annotations.example: He struggled not to laugh.

annotations.explain: file 作动词表示归档，separately 强调未与其他原件混作一处。
annotations.example: Please file these receipts separately.

annotations.explain: pass on 表示传递给下一个人；lead 指调查线索，不是已经证实的结论。
annotations.example: She passed the lead on to the police.

annotations.explain: leave something to somebody 表示托付后续责任，口语中常用于表示接手。
annotations.example: Leave the arrangements to me.

annotations.explain: let out a breath/sigh 是常见情绪动作描写。
annotations.example: He let out a sigh of relief.

annotations.explain: for once 表示与惯常情况不同地终于发生一次。
annotations.example: For once, the bus was on time.

annotations.explain: get in the way 是干扰事情进展的口语固定搭配。
annotations.example: Don't get in the way.

annotations.explain: Is there a difference between... 常用于对照；此处短句带吐槽。
annotations.example: Is there a difference between these two plans?

annotations.explain: before + 从句可表示在某行为发生前就采取措施。
annotations.example: Ask me before you start.

annotations.explain: be about to do 表示马上要做但尚未做的事。
annotations.example: I was about to argue, then changed my mind.

annotations.explain: out of breath 描述呼吸急促的状态，是常见固定表达。
annotations.example: She was out of breath after running.

annotations.explain: clutch 表紧握不放，动作常表现急迫或焦虑；prescription 是药方。
annotations.example: He stood there clutching a letter.

annotations.explain: pass on a message 是传话固定搭配，强调信息经他人转达。
annotations.example: Could you pass on a message?

annotations.explain: overhear 表示偶然听到别人的交谈，不等于正式听取证词。
annotations.example: I overheard them talking.

annotations.explain: batch of + 复数名词 表一批同类物品。
annotations.example: A batch of parcels arrived.

annotations.explain: stop dead 表示突然完全停下，与死亡无关。
annotations.example: She stopped dead in her tracks.

annotations.explain: 间接疑问句使用陈述语序，不是 what was it inside。
annotations.example: Nobody knew what was inside.

annotations.explain: before 用于截止时间；the third watch 是古代夜间时段，不应机械等同精确现代时钟时间。
annotations.example: The guards changed shifts before dawn.

annotations.explain: turn toward 描述身体或注意力转向某方向。
annotations.example: She turned toward the door.

annotations.explain: run back 表示原路跑回，with 表示陪同。
annotations.example: I ran back with my sister.

annotations.meaning: 我突然想到另一个问题
annotations.explain: a thought strikes somebody 是常见叙事表达，表示想法突然出现。
annotations.example: It suddenly struck me that I'd forgotten my keys.

annotations.phrase: allowed Nanny Zhou's husband to leave
annotations.explain: allow somebody to do 为常见动词结构，强调给予许可而非真正获得自由。
annotations.example: They allowed the patient to leave.

annotations.explain: find out who 后用陈述语序，可接过去完成/一般过去等时态。
annotations.example: They found out who had sent it.

annotations.explain: lead somebody to 可以指线索把某人引向某目标；straight 加强直接性。
annotations.example: The receipt led us straight to the supplier.

annotations.explain: succeed in doing 表成功做某事，介词 in 后接动名词；这里是否定。
annotations.example: They succeeded in finding the source.

annotations.explain: might well have + 过去分词，表达对过去结果的较强但非确定的推测。
annotations.example: We might well have made a mistake.

annotations.explain: in danger 表处于危险中，greater 是比较级，说明风险上升而非已经发生伤害。
annotations.example: The delay put the workers in greater danger.
